6018.d:
Objects and their functions no longer had any significance. All I perceived was perception itself, the hell of forms and figures devoid of human emotion and detached from the reality of my unreal environment. I was an instrument in a virtual world that constantly renewed its own meaningless image in a living world that was itself perceived outside of nature. And since the appearance of things was no longer definitive but limitless, this paradisiacal awareness freed me from the reality external to myself. The fire and the rose, as it were, became one. ― Federico Fellini

The tingling euphoria, splendid visuals and fractured vision – “will this ever end?" How things look cool, things sound good. 

Liquid Trips, 2022
Krinza M.

In full screen view, click on the graphic to download plottable SVG in A3 format.

The color palette used in here is supposed to represent 25 Stabilo Point fineliners. The color values don't come from any official specification, though.

Every minted edition consists of 3 color layers:

- black-ish (pen number 46) with constant hatching distance
- two color layers with randomly chosen color and distance values

If you have a pen plotter, you can jump straight into making a physical drawing. Please be aware, that physical plot might differ from the digital version due to the pen and paper color differences.

Each group ID consists of an index, a HEX color value, and a Stabilo Point pen color number. In Inkscape, just convert groups to layers, and you can start to plot (probably the best experience with AxiDraw A3 pen plotter).

If you don't own a plotter or you want a regular print, simply convert your SVG to raster format.

Two sets of artworks were selected for [TS-002]. They were selected by finding artworks with light or dark colors, before random selection.

There are light and dark color schemes. Sometimes they are mixed together and occasionally imagery with more vivid colors is sampled.

Open live and click artwork for pause/save functionality.

First icon: a binary representation of the transaction hash. 
Second icon: a meter denoting number of "trees"
Remaining icons: denote the boolean traits - sun, ring, and leaves.

Created in p5.js

Mandalas are ancient meditation devices. Simply focus on the centre of the mandala and allow it to bring peace to your mind. 
This mandala is created by drawing the path of circles within circles, each one moving faster than the one before.
There are eight simple colour combinations, with a greater likelihood of a black background.
There are two different degrees of symmetry possible and two different styles of drawing depending on how quickly the circles speed up within one another. They take between 20 and 40 seconds to draw, depending on complexity.

For an eternity, a dark path lay before us. Not one moment later and we were enveloped by light. A pregnant glow; it spanned the entirety of the Multiverse, ringing it like a deep bell.

🌐 A note on rarity and variety: 

Although there are many variations possible within this piece, they are on the subtler side.

As this is a highly temporal piece, these variations ask you to dive into the experience of the piece in order to fully appreciate them. Please proceed bearing this in mind.

Experiment with the aspect ratio of this piece using the ‘open live’ function below the viewport - it can be enjoyed elastically [as with my previous works here]. A square frame provides a more formal experience, while a widescreen view provides an anamorphic touch.

As with a handful of my works, I use .blend() within this piece; it causes some slight thinning and dimming to the preview capture. Once more, this still preview is to be considered a skeletal scan of a moment within this piece.

- Canvas orientation
- Color scheme
- Number of lanes
- Lane orientation
- Existence of a shadow on the circles
- Number of circles per lane
- Full circles or outlines only

Pressing 'p' will pause and restart the animation.
Pressing 's' will save a jpg of the work at it's current dimensions.

I hope you enjoy it as much as I do.

6142.d: This work is based is based on a public domain flat art illustration library called Humaaans, which is chosen here to exemplify contemporary big tech aesthetic. 6152.d:
This project is a reflection on transitions and the experience of moving through them.

Features
+ A, X, Y: Aspects of the equation for motion when mode is Searching
+ D: Depth of grid used for layout
+ M: Mode, either Resting or Searching
+ P: Speed of motion
+ S: State of form, either Isolate or Connect
+ T: Color theme
+ Z: Size

Interactive Controls (open live for best experience)
+ Press f to go full screen
+ Press space to toggle pause
+ Press m to toggle M feature
+ Press s to toggle S feature
+ Press up/down to change speed
+ Press left/right to change size
+ Press r to reset changes and start the animation from the beginning

Each minted edition has preset features based on the transaction hash, but the interactive controls allow for exploration of a subset of other possibilities, including some beyond the presets! Enjoy exploring. :)

--

Original artwork by metanivek, 2022.

6173.d:
What got me addicted to program visual art?
It's the feeling when your current level of expertise hits a challenge that just about exeeds your comfort zone. You set of in a valley of despair where the problem ahead seems 'too hard'.
You begin to inform yourself and learn from others who were stuck at a similiar problem.
You try things and a solution to the issue appears – your mind flies.
Hours later a warm tickling feeling spreads. Serendipitous bugs shift your trajectory.
Your body isn't present anymore, it's only brain, code and screen.
Suddenly the parameter space that grew over the last hours produced a first fully satisfying outcome. You did it!
Hectic explorations of the parameters follow, screenshots, exuberant git commit messages, dms to friends – until you realize it's 4:21 am and you fall into a short but deep, happy sleep.
On the way you follow 7 tweeps, read 3 papers, watch 11 tutorials, spend 48 hours on stackOverflow, learn about Goethe's color theory, tangent space, and The John Frum movement.

- The presence of feather, nostrils, broken beak, bloodshot/possessed eyes, glasses.

I'm now releasing the proper code and airdropping a piece to everyone who was holding a faulty piece at time of release.

The chosen background colors and their order are based on the transaction hash.

Following properties are also based on the transaction hash:
- Canvas orientation
- Color scheme
- Number of lanes
- Lane orientation
- Existence of a shadow on the circles
- Number of circles per lane
- Full circles or outlines only

Pressing 'p' will pause and restart the animation.
Pressing 's' will save a jpg of the work at it's current dimensions.

Generative image with animation (1024x1024px) Vanilla JS

This project is a string-art simulator which weaves some patterns in different layouts to make beautiful compositions which can be played from the beginning.
The main features of this generative collection are the several Patterns and Layouts which combined make a huge amount of variations.

“Pattern” defined as the instructions that the thread has to follow to weave the result.
"Layout" defined as the setup of the nails on the board.

The thread is always continuous without interruptions.

Features:

Pattern (21)
Layout (10)
Palette (25)
Layout Mirror (None, Horizontal, Vertical)
ThreadType: (Silk, Wool)
ThreadThickness: (Regular, Thick)

Controls:

[P] Play. 
[R] Result.
[U] Undo. 
[N] Nails. Show/Hide the nails.

[S] Download snapshot (may be slow or unresponsive)

You can weave yourself
Click to change the thread color

This project is an homage to Mary Everest Boole who, more than 100 years ago, used string art to teach math to children.

6198.d:
A Lissajous curve, also known as Lissajous figure or Bowditch curve, is the graph of a system of parametric equations which describe complex harmonic motion. This family of curves was investigated by Nathaniel Bowditch in 1815, and later in more detail in 1857 by Jules Antoine Lissajous (for whom it has been named).

The appearance of the figure is highly sensitive to the ratio Φx/Φy. For a ratio of 1, the figure is an ellipse. Other ratios produce more complicated curves, which are closed only if Φx/Φy is rational.

A generative art project is WebGL using Threejs. A rework of .rhizome, also here on FXHash.

The artwork gets generative procedurally over time, so resizing the browser would imply the canvas to be cleared out (and what has been painted to be lost).

Variations include:
- Number of particles (in order of rarity)
- Intensity of connections between the particles
- Colors (white, one color or multiple colors, in order of rarity)
- The radius
- The ratio Φx/Φy

A piece stepping away from control and leaning into minimalism, there are several factors at play to make your Esagoni unique. Both of the two hexagon colors are a random RGB value, at various luminosities.

The root of separation chooses which color takes the lead, between 1-100, 50 being evenly distributed.

The separation between the two colors can vary from 0-100, 0 is a 1% chance.

Modifiers can be either Circular or Hexagonal.

The scale of the hexagons on the grid varies from 1-100.

There is a 10% chance of a monochrome Esagoni, 5% respectively to both "Black on White" and "White on Black."


This piece can also be changed to infinite resolutions, for any frame or screen you'd like to display it on.

In live view, press:

'w' to view in 16:9

't' to view in 8x10

's' to view in 1x1

'f' to adapt to your own screen size

Double-click to save image

Enjoy :)

6229.d:
I tamed a 3D volumetric fractal to do this. Not an easy task, several hours of fine-tuning trying to reach what I want to express and please my eyes. Making sure that every iteration not only gives interesting results but they are part of the same concept. But when to stop? When it's finished? Well, maybe it never is. We are imperfect beings and so our art is. Everything always could be better, but sometimes we have to stop and accept that it's over, that it's the best we can do. And the best we can do it's good enough.

I want to dedicate this piece to Xiomara Elizabeth Martini.

In honor of the birthday of Vera Molnar. She is widely considered to be a pioneer of computer art and generative art, and is also one of the first women to use computers in her art practice. We have decide to create this little piece for the community. Hop you enjoy it. 

By 1959 she was making combinatorial images; in 1968 she would use a computer to create her first algorithmic drawings. In the 1960s she founded two groups in France concerned with the use of technology within the arts: the Groupe de Recherche d’Art Visuel and Art et Informatique. Her work has been widely collected by major museums; in 2007 she was named a Chevalier of Arts and Letters in France.
I work with some friends of mine Soro, programmer and art enthusiast  to create this piece inspire by « Structure A » of  1988.

We hope the community enjoy it ! 

Features :

Theme : dark, light
density : 1, 1.3, 1.6
quantity : 5, 7, 9, 11, 13, 15
colorSet : 5 colors palette selected over 360

Phazers is composed of:
32 Backgrounds
29 Background Patterns
32 Rings
31 Faces
16 Cheeks 
24 Mouths
13 Eyes
